sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Dordrecht, in Zuid-Holland, charges for street parking by zone, with hourly rates from 2.10 to 4.90 euros. The council adopted the parking tax ordinance on 16 December 2025, in force from 1 January 2026 [0]. From that date the street tariff is 4.90 euros an hour in zone 1A, 3.60 in zone 2A, 3.10 in zones 2B, 3, 5 and 6, and 2.10 in zone 4, with a day card of 39.20 euros in zone 1B, and zone 7 costs 1.00 euro for the first 24 hours and 0.50 euro an hour after that [1]. Short-stay sections cost 1.60 euros for the first 40 minutes, and the additional assessment for unpaid parking costs 82 euros [2]. Paid parking runs Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 22:00 and Sunday from 12:00 to 17:00 in the area enclosed by the Oude Maas, Weeskinderendijk, the railway lines, Noordendijk and the Wantij, with outer streets charged on shorter hours and a few streets, including Rie Mastenbroekweg, charged every day [3]. A half-year resident permit costs 84.08 euros for a first permit in area A and 249.12 euros for a second [4]. At most two resident permits are allowed per dwelling, with a waiting list when the sector maximum is reached [5], and the ceilings for the first half of 2026 were 2,380 in sector A and 800 in sector D, with no new second permits in sectors A, B, C, D and DD [10]. The car-free area in the centre is open to anyone for loading, unloading and dropping off passengers in set time windows [12]. For new buildings a zero parking norm applies in the pedestrian area of the old centre, with a 20 percent reduction within 500 metres of the central station [11].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The biggest project is a new Spuihaven garage. The municipality's tender documents of December 2025 say Dordrecht intends to demolish the dated Spuihaven car park and replace it with one of 726 spaces, as part of the Spuiboulevard area development, with demolition from 1 April 2027, handover on 2 October 2028 and target budgets of 600,000 euros for demolition and 25,338,000 euros for the new building, excluding VAT [6][7]. These are targets from a tender; a February 2026 answer says a revised foundation standard means the construction budget may be adjusted, and we do not know the outcome of the tender [8]. The college adopted updated rules for public charging on 17 March 2026, in force from 15 April 2026, under a concession with a charge point operator, which do not cover car parks and park-and-ride sites [9].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality itself is the contracting party for its car parks and the general terms of 2025 require payment before leaving [13]. The national parking register lists the municipality as operator of the garages Spuihaven (514 spaces), Energiehuis (326), Sportboulevard (626) and Riedijkshaven (46), and of the Gezondheidspark lot (572); APCOA Parking runs Visstraat and the Maasplaza lot, and the register entries are operator-reported and of mixed age [14]. The register also lists the P+R Markettenweg with 148 spaces under Nederlandse Spoorwegen, which is not one of the park-and-ride sites the municipality names in its parking rules for new buildings, Weeskinderendijk, Energiehuis and Gezondheidspark [11].

Our data cover the P+R Markettenweg, with 148 spaces, for about 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 27% on weekdays and 17% at weekends, with a peak of 95% on a Tuesday morning. The municipal garages and street parking are not in our data.
